knowledge_base.How to add a new work order:
To add a new work order, follow these steps:
 Step 1 - Navigate to the Work Order Management page by clicking on 'Work Orders' in the sidebar menu.
 Step 2 - Click the 'Add Work Order' button located in the top-right corner of the page.
 Step 3 - A modal dialog will open with multiple tabs for different sections.
 Step 4 - In the 'Basic Info' tab, enter the required fields: WO Number (required), Vendor ID, Project ID, Status (select from dropdown: PENDING, IN PROGRESS, COMPLETED, etc.), Description, Location, Municipality (select from dropdown), Area of Responsibility, and Assigned To.
 Step 5 - Check the 'VIP Project' switch if this is a VIP work order.
 Step 6 - Navigate to the 'Dates' tab and fill in relevant dates: Date Received Jacket (PS), Date Received Awarding WO, Date WMTRL, Date Scheduled, Date Received by VC, Actual Date Completed On Site, Date FCOMP, and Date COMP.
 Step 7 - Move to the 'Duration & Metrics' tab to enter duration calculations and performance metrics.
 Step 8 - In the 'Exclusions' tab, enter exclusion reasons if applicable, and set exclusion dates.
 Step 9 - Fill in COC & Audit information in the next tab, including audit dates and COC submission details.
 Step 10 - Complete the Contractor information tab with contractor-related dates and details.
 Step 11 - Review all information and click the 'Save' or 'Submit' button at the bottom of the modal.
 Step 12 - A success message will appear confirming the work order has been created. The new work order will now appear in the work orders table.
knowledge_base.How to edit an existing work order:
To edit an existing work order:
 Step 1 - Go to the Work Order Management page.
 Step 2 - Locate the work order you want to edit in the table (you can use filters or search to find it quickly).
 Step 3 - Click the Edit icon (pencil icon) in the Actions column for that work order row.
 Step 4 - The edit modal will open with all current data pre-filled in the form tabs.
 Step 5 - Navigate through the tabs and modify any fields you need to update.
 Step 6 - Click 'Save Changes' button when done.
 Step 7 - A success message will confirm the update. The table will refresh to show the updated information.
knowledge_base.How to delete a work order:
To delete a work order:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Work Order Management.
 Step 2 - Find the work order you want to delete in the table.
 Step 3 - Click the Delete icon (trash bin icon) in the Actions column.
 Step 4 - A confirmation dialog will appear asking 'Are you sure you want to delete this work order?'.
 Step 5 - Click 'Confirm' to proceed with deletion, or 'Cancel' to abort.
 Step 6 - Upon confirmation, the work order will be permanently deleted and removed from the table.
 Step 7 - A success message will display confirming the deletion.
knowledge_base.How to view work order details:
To view detailed information about a work order:
 Step 1 - Go to Work Order Management page.
 Step 2 - Locate the work order in the table.
 Step 3 - Click the View Details icon (eye icon) in the Actions column.
 Step 4 - A detailed view modal will open showing all information about the work order organized in sections: Basic Information, Date Tracking, Duration Metrics, Exclusions, COC Information, Audit Details, Contractor Information, Performance Metrics, and Supervisor Notes.
 Step 5 - Scroll through the sections to review all details.
 Step 6 - Click 'Close' or the X button to exit the view.
knowledge_base.How to view work order timeline:
To view the timeline of a work order:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Work Order Management.
 Step 2 - Find the work order in the table.
 Step 3 - Click the Timeline icon in the Actions column.
 Step 4 - A timeline view will open showing the chronological progression of the work order with all key dates and milestones displayed on a visual timeline.
 Step 5 - Review the timeline to understand the work order's history and progress.
 Step 6 - Close the timeline view when finished.
knowledge_base.How to filter work orders:
To filter work orders:
 Step 1 - On the Work Order Management page, click the 'Show Filters' button at the top of the page.
 Step 2 - A filters panel will expand showing multiple filter options.
 Step 3 - Use the Search field to search by WO Number, Description, or Location.
 Step 4 - Select a Status from the dropdown to filter by work order status (Pending, In Progress, Completed, etc.).
 Step 5 - Select a Municipality from the dropdown to filter by location.
 Step 6 - Use the VIP filter dropdown to show only VIP work orders, only Non-VIP, or All.
 Step 7 - The table will automatically update to show only work orders matching your filter criteria.
 Step 8 - To clear filters, either change the filter selections back to 'All' or click 'Hide Filters' and the page will reset.
knowledge_base.How to export work orders:
To export work order data:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Work Order Management page.
 Step 2 - Apply any filters if you want to export only specific work orders.
 Step 3 - Click the 'Export' button in the top action bar.
 Step 4 - The system will generate an Excel file containing all work orders (filtered or all).
 Step 5 - The file will automatically download to your computer's default download location.
 Step 6 - Open the Excel file to view the exported data with all work order fields in columns.
knowledge_base.How to handle system errors:
To import multiple work orders from a file:
 Step 1 - Prepare your import file using the correct template format (download the template first if you don't have it).
 Step 2 - On the Work Order Management page, click the 'Import' button.
 Step 3 - An import modal will open.
 Step 4 - Click 'Choose File' or drag and drop your Excel/CSV file into the upload area.
 Step 5 - The system will validate the file format and data.
 Step 6 - If validation passes, you'll see a preview of the data to be imported.
 Step 7 - Review the preview and click 'Confirm Import'.
 Step 8 - The system will process the import and display a success message showing how many records were imported.
 Step 9 - The work orders table will refresh to include the newly imported work orders. If there are errors, an error report will be displayed showing which rows failed validation and why.
knowledge_base.How to download work order template:
To download the work order template for importing:
 Step 1 - Go to Work Order Management page.
 Step 2 - Click the 'Template' button in the top action bar.
 Step 3 - An Excel template file will automatically download to your computer.
 Step 4 - Open the template file.
 Step 5 - You'll see column headers matching all work order fields with sample data in the first row.
 Step 6 - Replace the sample data with your actual work order information, following the format shown.
 Step 7 - Save the file and use it for importing work orders.
knowledge_base.How to switch between Card View and Exce:
To change the display format of work orders:
 Step 1 - On the Work Order Management page, look for the view tabs below the filters section.
 Step 2 - You'll see two tabs: 'Card View' (with a list icon) and 'Excel View' (with a table icon).
 Step 3 - Click 'Card View' to see work orders in a traditional table format with larger cells and action buttons.
 Step 4 - Click 'Excel View' to see work orders in a compact, Excel-like spreadsheet format with smaller cells and borders.
 Step 5 - The view preference will persist as you work with the page. Excel View is useful for seeing many records at once, while Card View provides easier reading and larger action buttons.
knowledge_base.How to add a new project:
To create a new project in the system:
 Step 1 - Navigate to the Projects page by clicking 'Projects' in the sidebar menu.
 Step 2 - Click the 'Add Project' or 'Create New Project' button (usually located in the top-right corner).
 Step 3 - A project creation modal will open.
 Step 4 - Fill in the Basic Information section: Enter Project Code (required, e.g., PROJ-2025-001), Enter Project Name (required), Select Vendor from the dropdown list, Select Sector from the dropdown, Select Assigned QI (Quality Inspector) from the dropdown.
 Step 5 - Enter project details: Enter Contract Value in Philippine Pesos, Select Start Date using the date picker, Select Expected Billing Date, Enter Project Location, Enter Project Description in the text area.
 Step 6 - Set project parameters: Select Priority level (Low, Medium, High, or Critical), Enter SLA Deadline Days (default is 7).
 Step 7 - Review all entered information for accuracy.
 Step 8 - Click 'Create Project' or 'Save' button.
 Step 9 - A success message will appear confirming the project creation.
 Step 10 - The new project will appear in the projects list and a unique Project ID will be automatically generated.
knowledge_base.How to edit project details:
To edit an existing project:
 Step 1 - Go to the Projects page.
 Step 2 - Locate the project you want to edit in the projects table.
 Step 3 - Click the Edit icon (pencil icon) in the actions column.
 Step 4 - The edit modal will open with all current project information pre-filled.
 Step 5 - Modify any fields that need updating: project name, vendor, dates, contract value, location, description, priority, or assigned personnel.
 Step 6 - Make sure all required fields remain filled.
 Step 7 - Click 'Save Changes' or 'Update Project' button.
 Step 8 - A confirmation message will display, and the project list will refresh with updated information.
knowledge_base.How to view project details:
To view complete project information:
 Step 1 - Navigate to the Projects page.
 Step 2 - Find the project in the list.
 Step 3 - Click the View Details icon (eye icon) or click on the project row.
 Step 4 - A detailed project view will open showing: Basic Information (code, name, vendor, sector), Financial Information (contract value, billing status), Timeline (start date, expected completion, actual completion), Assignment (QI, engineers, supervisors), Status and Progress, SLA compliance information, Associated documents, Penalty records, Workflow stages.
 Step 5 - Scroll through all sections to review complete project information.
 Step 6 - Click 'Close' or use the back button to return to the projects list.
knowledge_base.How to assign Quality Inspector to a pro:
To assign or change a QI for a project:
 Step 1 - Go to the Projects page.
 Step 2 - Locate the project that needs QI assignment.
 Step 3 - Click the Edit icon for that project.
 Step 4 - In the edit modal, find the 'Assigned QI' dropdown field.
 Step 5 - Click the dropdown and select the Quality Inspector from the list (QI users are filtered from the user list).
 Step 6 - The dropdown shows QI names in format: 'First Name Last Name'.
 Step 7 - Select the appropriate QI.
 Step 8 - Click 'Save Changes'.
 Step 9 - The QI assignment will be saved and the assigned QI will now be responsible for inspections on this project.
knowledge_base.How to update project status:
To change a project's status:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Projects.
 Step 2 - Find the project whose status you want to update.
 Step 3 - Click Edit for that project.
 Step 4 - Locate the Status field (usually in Basic Information section).
 Step 5 - Select the new status from the dropdown: Planning, In Progress, On Hold, Delayed, Completed, Cancelled, or other available statuses.
 Step 6 - If changing to 'Completed', ensure all required completion fields are filled (completion date, final documents, etc.).
 Step 7 - Click 'Save Changes'.
 Step 8 - The project status will update and this may trigger automated workflows such as: SLA tracking updates, notification to stakeholders, billing process initiation (if status is Completed), penalty calculations (if Delayed).
knowledge_base.How to search for projects:
To search and find specific projects:
 Step 1 - On the Projects page, look for the search bar usually located at the top of the page.
 Step 2 - Click in the search field.
 Step 3 - Type your search query. You can search by: Project Code, Project Name, Vendor Name, Location, or Description.
 Step 4 - As you type, the projects table will automatically filter to show matching results.
 Step 5 - The search is case-insensitive and searches across multiple fields.
 Step 6 - To clear the search, delete the text in the search field or click the X icon if available.
 Step 7 - The full projects list will be restored when search is cleared.
knowledge_base.How to filter projects by status:
To filter projects by their status:
 Step 1 - Go to Projects page.
 Step 2 - Look for the Filters section (click 'Show Filters' if not visible).
 Step 3 - Find the Status filter dropdown.
 Step 4 - Click the Status dropdown and select one of: All (to show all projects), Planning, In Progress, On Hold, Delayed, Completed, or Cancelled.
 Step 5 - The projects table will immediately filter to show only projects with the selected status.
 Step 6 - You can combine this with other filters (vendor, sector, date range) for more refined results.
 Step 7 - To reset, select 'All' from the Status dropdown.
knowledge_base.How to filter projects by vendor:
To view projects from a specific vendor:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Projects.
 Step 2 - Access the Filters panel.
 Step 3 - Locate the Vendor filter dropdown.
 Step 4 - Click the dropdown to see a list of all vendors.
 Step 5 - Select the vendor whose projects you want to view.
 Step 6 - The table will filter to show only projects assigned to that vendor.
 Step 7 - The vendor list shows vendor code and vendor name for easy identification.
 Step 8 - Select 'All Vendors' to remove the filter and show projects from all vendors.
knowledge_base.How to filter projects by sector:
To filter by geographic sector:
 Step 1 - On the Projects page, open the Filters section.
 Step 2 - Find the Sector filter dropdown.
 Step 3 - Click the dropdown to see all available sectors (e.g., Metro Manila North, Metro Manila South, Rizal, Cavite, Bulacan, etc.).
 Step 4 - Select the sector you want to view.
 Step 5 - The projects table will update to show only projects in the selected sector.
 Step 6 - This is useful for Sector Managers who need to focus on their area of responsibility.
 Step 7 - Choose 'All Sectors' to remove the filter.
knowledge_base.How to upload documents to a project:
To upload project documents:
 Step 1 - Navigate to the project's detail page or documents section.
 Step 2 - Click on 'Documents' or 'Upload Documents' button.
 Step 3 - A document upload modal will open.
 Step 4 - Select the Document Type from the dropdown (e.g., COC - Certificate of Completion, Technical Drawings, Permits, Photos, Invoices, Inspection Reports, Test Results, etc.).
 Step 5 - Click 'Choose File' or 'Browse' button.
 Step 6 - Select the document file from your computer (supported formats: PDF, DOCX, XLSX, JPG, PNG, etc.).
 Step 7 - Optionally, add a description or notes about the document.
 Step 8 - Set the document status if required (Draft, For Review, Approved).
 Step 9 - Click 'Upload' button.
 Step 10 - Wait for the upload progress bar to complete.
 Step 11 - A success message will confirm the upload.
 Step 12 - The document will now appear in the project's documents list with upload date, uploader name, and status.
knowledge_base.How to download project documents:
To download documents from a project:
 Step 1 - Go to the project detail page.
 Step 2 - Navigate to the Documents section or tab.
 Step 3 - You'll see a list of all documents associated with the project.
 Step 4 - Find the document you want to download.
 Step 5 - Click the Download icon (cloud download icon) next to the document.
 Step 6 - The document will begin downloading to your computer's default download location.
 Step 7 - You can download multiple documents by clicking download on each one.
 Step 8 - Some systems may also have a 'Download All' option to download all project documents as a ZIP file.
knowledge_base.How to approve documents:
To approve submitted documents:
 Step 1 - Navigate to the Documents section.
 Step 2 - Find the document that needs approval (usually marked with 'Pending Approval' or 'For Review' status).
 Step 3 - Click the View icon to review the document content.
 Step 4 - After reviewing, click the Approve button (usually a checkmark icon or 'Approve' button).
 Step 5 - A confirmation dialog may appear asking you to confirm approval.
 Step 6 - Optionally, add approval notes or comments.
 Step 7 - Click 'Confirm Approval'.
 Step 8 - The document status will change to 'Approved'.
 Step 9 - An automatic notification is sent to the document uploader and relevant stakeholders.
 Step 10 - Approved documents can then proceed in the workflow (e.g., approved COC allows billing process to continue).
knowledge_base.How to reject documents:
To reject documents that don't meet requirements:
 Step 1 - Go to Documents section.
 Step 2 - Review the document that needs action.
 Step 3 - Click the Reject button (usually an X icon or 'Reject' button).
 Step 4 - A rejection reason modal will appear.
 Step 5 - Enter a detailed rejection reason explaining why the document is not acceptable (required field).
 Step 6 - Specify what corrections or re-submissions are needed.
 Step 7 - Click 'Confirm Rejection'.
 Step 8 - The document status changes to 'Rejected'.
 Step 9 - An automatic notification is sent to the uploader with the rejection reason.
 Step 10 - The vendor or submitter must correct and re-upload the document to proceed.
knowledge_base.How to view vendor performance:
To review vendor performance metrics:
 Step 1 - Navigate to the Vendors section in the main menu.
 Step 2 - You'll see a list of all vendors with basic performance indicators.
 Step 3 - Click on a specific vendor name or View Details icon.
 Step 4 - The vendor performance dashboard will display showing: Compliance Score (0-100 rating), Total Projects assigned, Completed Projects, Delayed Projects, SLA Breaches count, Total Penalties amount, Average project completion time, On-time delivery percentage, Quality ratings, Recent project history, Penalty history.
 Step 5 - Review performance charts and graphs showing trends over time.
 Step 6 - Scroll down to see detailed metrics by project.
 Step 7 - You can export the vendor performance report using the Export button.
 Step 8 - Use this information to make decisions about future project assignments.
knowledge_base.How to add a new vendor:
To register a new vendor in the system:
 Step 1 - Go to Vendors page.
 Step 2 - Click 'Add Vendor' button.
 Step 3 - Fill in the vendor registration form: Enter Vendor Code (required, unique identifier), Enter Vendor Name (required), Enter Contact Person name, Enter Email Address, Enter Phone Number, Enter Business Address, Enter Tax ID Number (TIN), Select Vendor Type or Category, Set Initial Compliance Score (usually starts at 100 or default value), Check 'Active' checkbox to make vendor immediately available.
 Step 4 - Optionally upload vendor documents: Business permits, Licenses, Certifications, Insurance documents.
 Step 5 - Review all information for accuracy.
 Step 6 - Click 'Save' or 'Register Vendor'.
 Step 7 - A success message confirms vendor registration.
 Step 8 - The vendor is now available in all vendor dropdown lists across the system for project assignment.
knowledge_base.How to view vendor contact information:
To access vendor contact details:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Vendors page.
 Step 2 - Locate the vendor in the vendor list.
 Step 3 - Click on the vendor name or click View Details.
 Step 4 - The vendor profile page opens showing: Vendor Code and Name, Contact Person name and title, Email Address (clickable to send email), Phone Number (clickable to call), Business Address, Tax ID / TIN, Website (if provided), Emergency Contact, Authorized Representatives list.
 Step 5 - You can click email addresses to automatically open your email client with the vendor's address pre-filled.
 Step 6 - Phone numbers are clickable for quick calling.
 Step 7 - Use the Edit button if you need to update contact information.
knowledge_base.How to create an invoice:
To generate an invoice for a completed project:
 Step 1 - Ensure the project status is 'Completed' and all requirements are met.
 Step 2 - Navigate to Billing or Invoices section.
 Step 3 - Click 'Create Invoice' button.
 Step 4 - Select the Project from the dropdown list (only completed projects appear).
 Step 5 - The system auto-fills: Vendor information, Contract Value, Project details.
 Step 6 - Review and adjust if needed: Invoice Amount (contract value minus any penalties), Invoice Date (auto-set to current date), Due Date (auto-calculated based on payment terms).
 Step 7 - The system automatically calculates: Subtotal, Applied Penalties (if any), Total Penalties deduction, Final Invoice Amount.
 Step 8 - Review the Penalties section showing any deductions: SLA breaches, Quality issues, Delay penalties.
 Step 9 - Add invoice notes or special instructions if needed.
 Step 10 - Click 'Generate Invoice'.
 Step 11 - The invoice is created with a unique Invoice Number.
 Step 12 - The invoice PDF is automatically generated and available for download.
 Step 13 - Notification is sent to the vendor with invoice details.
 Step 14 - Invoice status is set to 'Issued'.
knowledge_base.How to view invoice details:
To review invoice information:
 Step 1 - Go to Invoices page.
 Step 2 - Find the invoice in the invoices table (you can search by invoice number, project, or vendor).
 Step 3 - Click on the invoice number or View Details icon.
 Step 4 - The invoice detail view displays: Invoice Number and Date, Project Information, Vendor Details, Contract Value, Applied Penalties (itemized list), Deductions breakdown, Final Payable Amount, Payment Status (Unpaid, Partially Paid, Paid), Payment Due Date, Payment History (if any payments made), Invoice PDF download link, Payment receipts (if available).
 Step 5 - You can download the invoice PDF by clicking the Download button.
 Step 6 - Review payment status and amounts.
 Step 7 - Click 'Close' to return to the invoices list.
knowledge_base.How to record invoice payment:
To record that an invoice has been paid:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Invoices page.
 Step 2 - Find the invoice that has been paid.
 Step 3 - Click Record Payment or Update Payment icon.
 Step 4 - A payment recording modal opens.
 Step 5 - Enter payment information: Payment Amount (can be partial or full), Payment Date (date payment was received), Payment Method (Bank Transfer, Check, Cash, etc.), Reference Number (check number, transaction ID, etc.), Bank Details (if applicable).
 Step 6 - If partial payment, the system calculates remaining balance.
 Step 7 - Optionally upload payment proof (receipt, bank statement, etc.).
 Step 8 - Add payment notes if needed.
 Step 9 - Click 'Record Payment'.
 Step 10 - The invoice status updates: to 'Partially Paid' if partial payment, to 'Paid' if full payment.
 Step 11 - Payment record is logged in payment history.
 Step 12 - Automatic notification sent to relevant parties.
 Step 13 - The vendor can view payment status in their portal.
knowledge_base.How to issue a penalty:
To create a penalty for non-compliance:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Penalties section.
 Step 2 - Click 'Issue Penalty' or 'Create Penalty' button.
 Step 3 - Fill in penalty information: Select Project from dropdown, Select Vendor (auto-filled based on project), Select Penalty Type: SLA Breach, Quality Issue, Safety Violation, Documentation Issue, or Other.
 Step 4 - Enter Violation Details: Description of the violation, Date of Violation, Severity Level (Low, Medium, High, Critical).
 Step 5 - The system can auto-calculate penalty amount using ML model based on: Violation type, Delay duration in days, Contract value, Vendor history.
 Step 6 - Or manually enter Penalty Amount if needed.
 Step 7 - Add supporting evidence: Upload photos, documents, or reports, Reference relevant work orders or milestones.
 Step 8 - Set Penalty Status to 'Draft' for review or 'Issued' to finalize.
 Step 9 - Add penalty notes or justification.
 Step 10 - Click 'Issue Penalty'.
 Step 11 - If status is 'Issued', a penalty memo is automatically generated and sent to the vendor.
 Step 12 - The penalty is reflected in: Vendor compliance score (decreased), Invoice calculations (deducted from payment), Penalty reports and analytics.
 Step 13 - Vendor receives notification and can view penalty details in their portal.
knowledge_base.How to view penalty details:
To review a penalty record:
 Step 1 - Go to Penalties page.
 Step 2 - Find the penalty in the penalties table (search by project, vendor, or date).
 Step 3 - Click on the penalty reference number or View Details icon.
 Step 4 - The penalty detail view shows: Penalty ID and Reference Number, Project and Vendor Information, Penalty Type and Category, Violation Date and Description, Severity Level, Penalty Amount, Calculation Method (ML-predicted or manual), Supporting Documents and Evidence, Penalty Status (Draft, Issued, Paid, Waived, Disputed), Issue Date, Payment Status, Dispute Information (if applicable), Status history and timeline.
 Step 5 - You can download the penalty memo PDF.
 Step 6 - Review any dispute notes if vendor contested the penalty.
 Step 7 - View related invoices where this penalty was applied.
knowledge_base.How to waive a penalty:
To waive or cancel a penalty:
 Step 1 - Navigate to Penalties section.
 Step 2 - Locate the penalty to be waived.
 Step 3 - Click the Edit or Waive button.
 Step 4 - A waiver form opens.
 Step 5 - Select Waiver Reason from dropdown: Vendor provided valid justification, Circumstances beyond vendor control, First-time minor violation, Management decision, or Other.
 Step 6 - Enter detailed Waiver Justification explaining why penalty is being waived.
 Step 7 - Attach any supporting documents if needed.
 Step 8 - Get required approvals if policy requires supervisor or manager approval.
 Step 9 - Click 'Waive Penalty'.
 Step 10 - Penalty status changes to 'Waived'.
 Step 11 - If penalty was already deducted from an invoice, adjustments may be needed: Create credit note or Adjust next invoice.
 Step 12 - Vendor compliance score is adjusted back (penalty impact removed).
 Step 13 - Automatic notification sent to vendor confirming waiver.
 Step 14 - Waiver is logged in penalty history for audit trail.
knowledge_base.How to dispute a penalty:
For vendors to dispute a penalty:
 Step 1 - Vendor logs into Vendor Portal.
 Step 2 - Goes to Penalties section.
 Step 3 - Finds the penalty they want to dispute.
 Step 4 - Clicks 'Dispute Penalty' button.
 Step 5 - A dispute form opens with fields: Dispute Reason (required - dropdown with options), Detailed Explanation (text area - required), Supporting Evidence (file upload section).
 Step 6 - Vendor selects dispute reason: Incorrect violation date, Delay not vendor's fault, Force majeure circumstances, Incorrect penalty amount, Documentation error, or Other.
 Step 7 - Vendor writes detailed explanation of why they believe penalty is incorrect or unfair.
 Step 8 - Vendor uploads supporting documents: Photos showing actual conditions, Third-party reports, Correspondence, Weather reports, or other evidence.
 Step 9 - Vendor selects Preferred Resolution: Full waiver, Partial reduction, Payment plan, or Other arrangement.
 Step 10 - Vendor clicks 'Submit Dispute'.
 Step 11 - Penalty status changes to 'Disputed'.
 Step 12 - Dispute is routed to supervisor or manager for review.
 Step 13 - Vendor receives acknowledgment notification.
 Step 14 - Supervisor reviews dispute and supporting evidence.
 Step 15 - Supervisor makes decision: Approve (waive penalty), Partially approve (reduce amount), or Deny dispute.
 Step 16 - Vendor is notified of decision with explanation.
 Step 17 - If approved, penalty is waived or adjusted. If denied, penalty remains and vendor can appeal to higher management if policy allows.
knowledge_base.How to create a QI inspection:
For Quality Inspectors to create an inspection record:
 Step 1 - QI logs into their account.
 Step 2 - Navigates to Inspections or My Inspections page.
 Step 3 - Clicks 'New Inspection' or 'Create Inspection' button.
 Step 4 - Selects the Project from dropdown (shows projects assigned to this QI).
 Step 5 - System auto-fills project details: Work Order Number, Vendor, Location.
 Step 6 - Selects Inspection Type from dropdown: Pre-construction, In-progress, Final, Re-inspection, Quality Audit, Safety Inspection, or other types.
 Step 7 - Sets Scheduled Date for the inspection.
 Step 8 - Enters Inspection Location if different from project address.
 Step 9 - Adds inspection scope or checklist items.
 Step 10 - Clicks 'Create Inspection'.
 Step 11 - Inspection is created with status 'Scheduled'.
 Step 12 - Inspection appears in QI's daily task list.
 Step 13 - Reminders are set for the scheduled date.
 Step 14 - On inspection day, QI conducts the site visit and records findings.
knowledge_base.How to record inspection results:
To record findings from a completed inspection:
 Step 1 - QI opens their scheduled inspection from My Inspections list.
 Step 2 - Clicks 'Start Inspection' or 'Record Results'.
 Step 3 - Inspection form opens with sections: General Information, Checklist Items, Findings, Photos/Evidence.
 Step 4 - Goes through each checklist item and marks: Pass, Fail, Not Applicable, or Conditional Pass.
 Step 5 - For failed items: Adds description of the issue, Selects severity (Minor, Major, Critical), Adds corrective action required.
 Step 6 - Takes photos of inspection areas: Click 'Add Photo', Use camera or upload from device, Add caption to each photo describing what it shows.
 Step 7 - Records overall inspection findings in notes section.
 Step 8 - Selects Overall Inspection Result: Passed (all items acceptable), Failed (critical issues found), Conditional (minor issues, re-inspection needed).
 Step 9 - If Conditional or Failed: Lists all corrective actions needed, Sets deadline for corrections, Schedules re-inspection date if needed.
 Step 10 - Adds inspector notes and recommendations.
 Step 11 - Signs inspection digitally if required.
 Step 12 - Clicks 'Submit Inspection Results'.
 Step 13 - Inspection status updates to 'Completed'.
 Step 14 - Automatic notifications sent to: Vendor (with findings and required corrections), Project supervisor, Assigned engineers.
 Step 15 - If inspection failed, project workflow may be blocked until issues are resolved and re-inspection passes.
 Step 16 - Inspection results are logged in project history.
 Step 17 - QI performance metrics are updated (inspection completed on time).
knowledge_base.How to view QI performance:
To review Quality Inspector performance metrics:
 Step 1 - Navigate to QI Management or QI Performance section (accessible to supervisors and managers).
 Step 2 - Select a specific QI from the list or view all QIs.
 Step 3 - Performance dashboard displays: Assigned Inspections count, Completed Inspections count, Pending Inspections, Overdue Inspections, On-time Completion Rate (%), Daily Target Achievement, Average Inspection Time, Pass/Fail/Conditional ratios, Quality Rating Score, Inspector Workload (current vs. capacity).
 Step 4 - View graphical representations: Monthly inspection trends, Pass/fail rate trends over time, Workload distribution charts.
 Step 5 - See detailed inspection history: Recent inspections list, Inspection dates and results, Projects covered, Time taken per inspection.
 Step 6 - Review performance against targets: Daily inspection targets (calculated based on historical performance), Monthly targets, Year-to-date performance.
 Step 7 - Check reasons for missed targets if any: Workload too high, Project delays, Insufficient resources, Training needed.
 Step 8 - Use this data to: Balance workload distribution, Identify training needs, Recognize high performers, Address performance issues.
 Step 9 - Export performance reports for documentation.
knowledge_base.How to check SLA compliance:
To monitor Service Level Agreement compliance:
 Step 1 - Navigate to SLA Tracking or SLA Compliance page.
 Step 2 - View SLA dashboard showing: Total Active SLAs, Breached SLAs count, At-Risk SLAs (approaching deadline), Compliance Rate percentage.
 Step 3 - Filter SLAs by: Project, Vendor, SLA Type (document submission, inspection, completion, etc.), Status (Met, Breached, Pending).
 Step 4 - Click on a specific SLA or project to view detailed SLA tracking.
 Step 5 - For each SLA milestone, see: Target completion date, Actual completion date (if completed), Days remaining (if pending), Status indicator (green = on track, yellow = at risk, red = breached), Associated workflow stage.
 Step 6 - View breach details if SLA was not met: Delay duration in days, Reason for delay, Responsible party, Escalation history, Penalty calculation (if applicable).
 Step 7 - Review SLA rules that apply: Target duration in days, Escalation triggers, Penalty rules, Required actions.
 Step 8 - Check automated escalations: When SLA is at risk (usually 80% of time elapsed), system sends warning notifications, If SLA breached, escalation sent to supervisor/manager, Repeated breaches trigger higher-level escalations.
 Step 9 - For projects at risk: View recommended actions, Send manual reminders, Escalate to management if needed.
 Step 10 - Export SLA compliance reports for management review.
knowledge_base.How to set SLA rules:

 Step 3 - For each SLA type, configure: Target Duration: Enter number of days (can be decimal, e.g., 0.5 for 12 hours), Warning Threshold: Percentage of time before warning (e.g., 80% = warning at 80% of duration), Critical Threshold: When SLA is at critical risk (e.g., 95%), Start Trigger: What event starts the SLA clock (e.g., 'COC submitted' starts inspection SLA), End Trigger: What event stops the clock (e.g., 'Inspection completed'), Exclusions: Exclude weekends (yes/no), Exclude holidays (yes/no), Exclude specific delay reasons.
 Step 4 - Set SLA by project type: Standard projects: Default SLA duration, VIP projects: Shorter duration (e.g., 50% of standard), Emergency projects: Expedited timeline, Large projects: Extended duration.
 Step 5 - Configure notifications: At warning threshold (80%): Send reminder to responsible person, Send FYI to supervisor. At critical threshold (95%): Send urgent reminder, Escalate to next level. At breach (100%): Send breach notification to all stakeholders, Auto-escalate to management, Trigger penalty calculation if applicable.
 Step 6 - Set escalation rules: First Level: Notify team leader after X hours of delay, Second Level: Notify sector manager after Y hours, Third Level: Notify senior management after Z hours, Include progressively more people in each escalation.
 Step 7 - Configure business hours: Define work hours (e.g., 8 AM - 5 PM), SLA clock may pause outside business hours depending on configuration, Set timezone for SLA calculations.
 Step 8 - Define holidays and non-working days: Import company holiday calendar, Add sector-specific holidays, SLA timers pause on these dates.
 Step 9 - Set exceptions and overrides: Allow manual SLA extension with approval, Define who can extend SLAs, Require justification for extensions, Log all extensions for audit.
 Step 10 - Configure penalty rules linked to SLA: Auto-calculate penalty for breaches (yes/no), Penalty rate (e.g., ₱500 per day past SLA), Maximum penalty cap (% of contract value), Grace period before penalties apply, First-time offender leniency.
 Step 11 - Test SLA configuration: Create test project, Trigger SLA start event, Verify timers start correctly, Test warnings at correct thresholds, Verify escalations work, Check penalty calculations.
 Step 12 - Monitor SLA performance: Dashboard shows: SLA compliance rate, Average time to complete, Frequent breaches (by type, vendor, sector), Use data to adjust SLA targets if unrealistic.
 Step 13 - Document SLA policies: Create SLA policy document explaining all timelines, Share with all stakeholders and vendors, Include in vendor contracts, Review and update SLAs quarterly.
knowledge_base.How to handle system errors:
What to do when encountering errors:
 Step 1 - Read the error message carefully: Note exact error text, Note error code if shown, Note what you were trying to do when error occurred.
 Step 2 - Common error types and solutions: 'Permission Denied' error: You don't have access to this function, Contact administrator to request permission, Or verify you're using correct account. 'Validation Error' messages: Check form fields for red highlights, Read specific field error messages, Correct the highlighted fields, Ensure required fields are filled, Ensure correct data format (dates, numbers, etc.), Try submitting again. 'Network Error' or 'Connection Lost': Check your internet connection, Try refreshing the page, Try logging out and back in, Clear browser cache and cookies, Try different browser. 'File Upload Failed': Check file size is under limit (usually 10-20MB), Check file type is allowed (PDF, JPG, PNG, Excel, Word), Ensure filename has no special characters, Try compressing large files, Try different file format. 'Session Expired': You were inactive too long, Click to log in again, Unsaved work may be lost - save frequently.
 Step 3 - Try basic troubleshooting: Refresh the page (F5 or refresh button), Clear browser cache: Press Ctrl+Shift+Delete, Select cached images and files, Clear data, Log out and log back in, Try in different browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge), Try in incognito/private window, Restart your browser completely.
 Step 4 - If error persists: Take screenshot of error message, Note exact steps to reproduce error, Note time when error occurred, Contact system support or administrator with: Screenshot of error, Description of what you were doing, Your username (not password), Browser and version you're using, Time of error.
 Step 5 - System maintenance errors: 'System Under Maintenance' page: System is being updated, Try again in timeframe shown, Check email for maintenance notifications. Scheduled maintenance usually announced in advance.
 Step 6 - Data not loading: Check your network connection, Try waiting a moment for slow queries, Check if filters are too restrictive (preventing results), Try clearing filters and searching again, Refresh the data using refresh button if available.
 Step 7 - Critical data loss prevention: System should auto-save form data periodically, If browser crashes, data may be recovered on return, Save work frequently when entering large amounts of data, Use 'Save as Draft' if available before final submit, Keep local backup of important data you're entering.
 Step 8 - Report persistent bugs: Document reproducible bugs, Check if bug already reported, Submit bug report to IT/development team including: Detailed steps to reproduce, Expected vs. actual behavior, Screenshots or screen recording, Your user role and permissions, Browser and operating system info.
 Step 9 - Workarounds while waiting for fix: Use alternate method if available, Export and import data if entry is failing, Contact support for manual processing, Check if issue is browser-specific (try different browser).
 Step 10 - System status page: Some systems have status page showing: Current system status (operational, degraded, down), Active incidents and resolutions, Scheduled maintenance, Performance metrics, Check this page if experiencing issues.

knowledge_base.What is the Smart Vendor Monitoring Syst: The Smart Vendor Monitoring System is a comprehensive platform designed to monitor and manage vendor performance, track project progress, enforce SLAs, calculate penalties, and provide analytics for MERALCO's vendor management operations. It integrates automation and AI to streamline work order closing processes, enhance quality assurance, and ensure timely vendor billing.
knowledge_base.Show me system statistics: The system currently manages multiple projects across various sectors. You can view detailed statistics including total projects, active vendors, delayed projects, SLA breaches, and penalty amounts in the dashboard.
knowledge_base.List delayed projects: To view delayed projects, go to the Projects section and filter by 'Delayed' status. The system tracks delays automatically and flags projects that are behind schedule based on their target completion dates.
knowledge_base.Which projects are at risk?: Projects at risk are those with high risk scores (above 0.7) or multiple SLA breaches. The ML model analyzes factors like project status, priority, contract value, vendor compliance score, and days since start to predict delay probability.
knowledge_base.What are the main causes of project dela: Common delay factors include: weather conditions, material shortages, permit delays, design changes, resource unavailability, site access issues, quality problems, and vendor performance issues. The system tracks all delay factors for analytics.
knowledge_base.How does the penalty system work?: Penalties are calculated based on violation type and delay duration. The system uses an ML model trained on historical data to predict penalty amounts. Penalties can be in Draft, Issued, Paid, Waived, or Disputed status. The system includes a penalty enforcement module that automatically tracks compliance, flags overdue tasks, and generates penalty memos to discourage repeated vendor delays.
knowledge_base.Explain SLA tracking: SLA (Service Level Agreement) tracking monitors project milestones against defined timelines. Each workflow stage has SLA rules with target durations. The system automatically flags breaches and can escalate to appropriate personnel.
knowledge_base.What are the system features?: Key features include: Automated Dashboard with real-time tracking and KPI visuals, Automated Email and Notification System with scheduled reminders, AI Integration with natural language chatbot, Project Management, Vendor Performance Tracking, SLA Monitoring, Document Management, Quality Inspections, Penalty Management, Billing & Invoicing, Analytics & Reporting, and AI-powered Predictions.
knowledge_base.How do quality inspections work?: Quality Inspectors (QI) are assigned inspections based on project milestones. They have daily targets and must complete inspections by scheduled dates. Results are recorded as Passed, Failed, or Conditional, affecting project progression. The system includes a workload capability tracker that calculates audit targets based on historical performance and summarizes reasons for unmet targets.
knowledge_base.What is the vendor compliance score?: Vendor compliance score (0-100) reflects overall vendor performance based on on-time delivery, quality ratings, SLA adherence, and penalty history. Higher scores indicate better performance.
knowledge_base.How can I view vendor performance?: Navigate to the Vendors section to see performance metrics including compliance scores, total projects, delayed projects, SLA breaches, and penalty amounts. You can sort by performance to identify top and underperforming vendors.
knowledge_base.What workflows are tracked?: The system tracks workflows for: Project Approval, Design Review, Material Procurement, Construction, QI Inspections, Testing & Commissioning, Documentation, and Project Closeout. Each stage has defined SLAs and assigned personnel.
knowledge_base.How are penalties calculated?: The ML model considers violation type (delay, quality issue, safety violation, documentation issue) and delay duration in days. For example, a 30-day delay might result in a penalty of ₱50,000-₱200,000 depending on project value and contract terms.
knowledge_base.What reports are available?: Available reports include: Project Status Summary, Vendor Performance Report, Delay Analysis, SLA Breach Report, Penalty Summary, Invoice Status, QI Performance, and Monthly Trends. Reports can be filtered by date range, sector, or vendor. The system enables automated report generation (weekly/monthly) that summarizes project statuses, vendor compliance, SLA breaches, billing progress, and other key metrics for management decision-making.
knowledge_base.How do I create a new project?: To create a project, go to Projects > Add New. Enter project details including code, name, sector, vendor, start/end dates, contract value, and priority. The system will automatically set up workflow stages and SLA tracking.
knowledge_base.What is the escalation process?: When SLAs are breached or issues arise, the system automatically escalates to designated personnel based on escalation rules. Team Leaders receive first-level escalations, then Sector Managers, and finally System Administrators.
knowledge_base.How do vendors submit documents?: Vendors access the Vendor Portal to upload required documents. The system tracks submission deadlines and flags overdue documents. Documents undergo approval workflow by assigned personnel (Engineers, QI, or Supervisors). Automated reminders are sent to vendors to ensure timely submission of COC and other required documents.
knowledge_base.What are the user roles?: System roles include: System Administrator, Team Leader, Sector Manager, Engineer, Vendor Representative, Quality Inspector, Clerk, Engineering Aide, and WO Supervisor. Each role has specific permissions and dashboard views.
knowledge_base.How is project delay predicted?: The ML model analyzes project characteristics (status, priority, contract value, vendor compliance, days since start, risk score) and compares them to historical patterns to predict delay probability with risk levels: Low (<40%), Medium (40-70%), High (>70%). The AI-powered features provide predictive analytics for delay forecasting.
knowledge_base.What notifications are sent?: The system sends notifications for: SLA breaches, approaching deadlines, document submissions, inspection schedules, escalations, penalty issuance, and invoice due dates. Users can configure notification preferences. The automated email and notification system sends scheduled reminders to vendors and internal teams, with SMS or push alerts for urgent cases.
knowledge_base.How do I dispute a penalty?: Vendors can submit disputes through the Vendor Portal. Include dispute reason, supporting documents, and preferred resolution. Disputes are reviewed by assigned personnel and can be approved, rejected, or result in penalty waiver.
knowledge_base.What is the billing process?: After project completion, invoices are generated based on contract value minus any applicable penalties. Invoices go through approval workflow before being issued to vendors. Payment status is tracked (Unpaid, Partially Paid, Paid). The system ensures timely billing by automating the process from project completion to vendor billing.
knowledge_base.How are sectors organized?: Projects are organized by geographic sectors (e.g., Metro Manila North, Metro Manila South, Rizal, Cavite, Bulacan). Each sector has a designated Sector Manager who oversees all projects in that area. The system is being piloted at Meralco Networks Paranaque Sector Construction 1 Office.
knowledge_base.What is the document compliance tracking: The system tracks required documents for each project phase. It monitors submission deadlines, approval status, and flags overdue documents. Compliance affects project progression and vendor scores. The system addresses vendor submission delays where vendors often fail to submit required COC and documents on time.
knowledge_base.How do I view my tasks?: Your role-specific dashboard shows assigned tasks including: pending approvals, scheduled inspections, overdue documents, escalations, and projects requiring attention. Tasks are prioritized by urgency and SLA status.
knowledge_base.What analytics are available?: Analytics include: Project trends over time, Delay factor analysis, Vendor performance comparison, SLA compliance rates, Penalty trends, Budget vs. Actual costs, Sector-wise statistics, and QI performance metrics.
knowledge_base.How is vendor feedback handled?: Stakeholders can submit vendor feedback rating service quality, responsiveness, and professionalism (1-5 stars). Feedback is reviewed and affects vendor compliance scores and future project assignments.
knowledge_base.What is the change log?: The system maintains detailed audit logs tracking all data changes including who made changes, when, and what was modified. This ensures accountability and helps with compliance audits.
knowledge_base.How do I export data?: Most data tables include export options for Excel, CSV, or PDF formats. Select the data you want to export, choose format, and click Export. Large datasets may be processed in the background.
knowledge_base.What are project milestones?: Milestones are key checkpoints in project delivery (e.g., Design Approval, Material Delivery, Construction 50%, QI Inspection, Testing Complete). Each milestone has target dates and completion tracking.
knowledge_base.How is risk score calculated?: Risk score (0-10) is calculated based on: project complexity, contract value, vendor history, location challenges, resource availability, and external factors. Higher scores indicate higher risk of delays or issues.
knowledge_base.What problems does the system solve?:
The system addresses four main problems:
 (1) Vendor submission delays for COC and required documents,
 (2) Weak penalty enforcement for SLA breaches,
 (3) Overloaded QI monitoring making it difficult to meet audit targets, and
 (4) Limited process visibility with lack of integrated dashboard and real-time tracking.
knowledge_base.What is the purpose of this system?: The system aims to develop a Smart Vendor Project Monitoring System that automates and streamlines the process from project completion to vendor billing. It addresses common delays in document submission, inspection, and penalty enforcement through an integrated dashboard, automated reminders, and AI-assisted tracking.
knowledge_base.What are the main objectives?:
The main objectives are:
 (1) Automate project monitoring through centralized dashboard,
 (2) Implement automated email and notification system,
 (3) Integrate AI-powered features like chatbot and predictive analytics,
 (4) Develop SLA monitoring and penalty enforcement,
 (5) Incorporate QI workload capability tracker,
 (6) Enable automated report generation, and
 (7) Evaluate system effectiveness in improving work order closing timelines.
knowledge_base.What AI features are included?: AI features include: Natural language chatbot for instant project inquiries, Historical query handler for project data retrieval, Predictive analytics for delay forecasting, Automated suggestions for corrective actions and process improvements, and ML models for penalty prediction and risk assessment.
knowledge_base.How does the chatbot work?: The AI-powered chatbot allows users to make instant inquiries about projects using natural language. It can retrieve historical project data, answer questions about project status, provide information about vendors, explain system features, and guide users through various processes.
knowledge_base.What is the dashboard view like?: The automated dashboard provides real-time project tracking with KPI visuals and status indicators. It is designed to be both large-monitor and mobile-friendly, allowing stakeholders to access project information from anywhere. The dashboard displays project statuses, vendor compliance, SLA breaches, and workload distribution.
knowledge_base.How does the system improve efficiency?: The system improves efficiency by reducing manual tasks, automating reminders and notifications, providing real-time visibility into project status, enabling faster decision-making through analytics, reducing billing cycle times, and improving vendor compliance through consistent penalty enforcement.
knowledge_base.What is the research hypothesis?: The null hypothesis states that implementation does not significantly improve efficiency. The alternative hypothesis states that implementation significantly improves the efficiency of work order closing, vendor compliance, and timeliness of billing compared to the current manual process.
knowledge_base.What is the implementation timeline?: The implementation follows a 6-month timeline: Month 1 - Requirement Analysis & Data Collection, Month 2 - System Design, Month 3 - Development, Month 4 - Pilot Testing, Month 5 - Deployment, Month 6 - Evaluation & Final Report.
knowledge_base.What are the implementation phases?: Phase 1: Requirement Analysis & System Design, Phase 2: System Development, Phase 3: Pilot Testing & Feedback, Phase 4: Full Deployment & Training, Phase 5: Post-Implementation Evaluation. Each phase has specific deliverables and outcomes.
knowledge_base.What is the research design methodology?: The study employs a Developmental Research Design (R&D) combined with a Descriptive-Evaluative Approach. The R&D design is appropriate for the design, development, and testing of the system, while the Descriptive-Evaluative component measures and describes the system's impact.
knowledge_base.How is data gathered for evaluation?:
Data is gathered through four stages:
 (1) Pre-Development Stage with interviews, surveys, and historical data collection,
 (2) System Development Stage using Agile approach with feedback loops,
 (3) System Testing & Implementation Stage with pilot deployment, and
 (4) Evaluation Stage with post-implementation surveys and KPI analysis.
knowledge_base.What instruments are used for evaluation: Evaluation instruments include: Survey Questionnaire for user satisfaction, System Usage Logs to track real-time usage and compliance rates, KPI Metrics comparing pre- and post-implementation data, and Interview Guide for collecting qualitative insights during pilot testing.
knowledge_base.Who is the target user base?: Target users include: Team Leaders, WO Supervisors, Quality Inspectors, Vendor Representatives, Clerks, Engineering Aides, Sector Managers, Engineers, and System Administrators. The system is specifically designed for personnel involved in work order closing and vendor management.
knowledge_base.What is the sampling technique used?: Purposive Sampling is used since only participants directly involved in work order closing and vendor management are included. This includes Team Leaders, WO Supervisors, Quality Inspectors, Vendor Representatives, Clerks, and Engineering Aides.
knowledge_base.What are the expected benefits?: Expected benefits include: Reduced vendor billing delays, Improved compliance and accountability, Enhanced visibility and real-time monitoring, Reduced manual workload for QI teams, Faster decision-making through data-driven insights, Consistent penalty enforcement, and Better resource allocation.
knowledge_base.How does the system handle backjobs?: The automated notification system sends scheduled reminders to vendors and internal teams to ensure faster resolution of backjobs. The dashboard provides visibility into pending work and overdue tasks, allowing teams to prioritize and address backjobs systematically.
knowledge_base.What is QI workload management?: The system incorporates a workload capability tracker for QI teams that calculates audit targets based on historical performance data. It summarizes reasons for unmet targets and supports data-driven corrective measures, helping to manage and optimize QI workload effectively.
knowledge_base.How does automation improve the work ord: Automation streamlines the work order closing process by eliminating manual tracking, automating document submission reminders, providing real-time status updates, automatically flagging delays and SLA breaches, generating reports automatically, and reducing the time from project completion to vendor billing.
knowledge_base.What is the theoretical framework?:
The theoretical framework is based on four key areas:
 (1) Automation in Vendor Management showing 25-45% efficiency gains,
 (2) AI in Project Tracking and Predictive Monitoring for real-time monitoring and alerts,
 (3) Automation in Billing and Invoice Systems to reduce errors and processing time, and
 (4) SLA Monitoring, Escalation & Penalty Automation to ensure compliance.
knowledge_base.What does the literature review show?: The literature review shows that automation reduces manual tasks and compliance gaps with international studies demonstrating 25-45% efficiency gains. AI enables real-time monitoring and predictive alerts, billing automation reduces errors and processing time, and SLA monitoring with automation reduces vendor delays.
knowledge_base.What is the conceptual framework?: The conceptual framework integrates automation and AI to transform the manual, fragmented work order closing process into an efficient, automated system. It connects input factors (vendor data, project data, historical data) through processing (automation, AI, analytics) to outputs (improved efficiency, compliance, timely billing).
knowledge_base.How does the system prevent repeated del: The system prevents repeated delays through consistent penalty enforcement, automated reminders before deadlines, real-time tracking and escalation of overdue tasks, vendor compliance scoring that affects future assignments, and predictive analytics that identify at-risk projects early for proactive intervention.
knowledge_base.What makes this system 'smart'?: The system is 'smart' because it uses AI and machine learning for predictive analytics, automated decision-making for escalations and notifications, intelligent workload distribution for QI teams, pattern recognition to identify delay trends, natural language processing for the chatbot, and continuous learning from historical data to improve predictions.
knowledge_base.Why is real-time monitoring important?: Real-time monitoring is important because it enables immediate visibility into project status, allows for proactive issue resolution before delays occur, supports faster decision-making, improves stakeholder communication, helps identify bottlenecks quickly, and ensures accountability at all levels of the process.
knowledge_base.How does the system support data-driven: The system supports data-driven decisions by providing comprehensive analytics on project performance, vendor compliance trends, delay patterns, resource utilization, historical comparisons, predictive insights, and automated reports that highlight key metrics and areas requiring attention.
knowledge_base.What is the impact on billing timelines?: The system significantly reduces billing timelines by automating the process from project completion to invoice generation, eliminating manual document tracking, reducing approval cycles through automated workflows, ensuring all requirements are met before billing, and providing clear visibility into billing status.
knowledge_base.How are COC documents tracked?: Certificate of Completion (COC) documents are tracked through the document management system. The system monitors submission deadlines, sends automated reminders to vendors, flags overdue COCs, tracks approval workflows, and ensures COC completion before proceeding with billing.
knowledge_base.What happens when SLA is breached?: When SLA is breached, the system automatically flags the violation, sends notifications to relevant stakeholders, escalates according to predefined rules, calculates applicable penalties, generates penalty memos, and updates vendor compliance scores. The breach is also recorded in analytics for trend analysis.
knowledge_base.Can I customize notification preferences: Yes, users can configure their notification preferences including which events trigger notifications (SLA breaches, deadlines, submissions), delivery method (email, SMS, push notification), frequency of reminders, and escalation thresholds. This ensures users receive relevant notifications without being overwhelmed.
knowledge_base.How does the system ensure accountabilit: The system ensures accountability through detailed audit logs tracking all actions, role-based permissions limiting access, automated escalations when deadlines are missed, penalty enforcement for non-compliance, performance scoring for vendors and personnel, and transparent reporting visible to all stakeholders.
knowledge_base.What is the vendor portal?: The vendor portal is a dedicated interface where vendor representatives can view assigned projects, upload required documents, track submission deadlines, receive notifications and reminders, submit penalty disputes, view compliance scores, and access project-specific information and requirements.
knowledge_base.How does mobile-friendly access help?: Mobile-friendly access allows stakeholders to monitor projects and receive notifications on-the-go, approve documents from anywhere, check project status in the field, respond to escalations quickly, and access critical information without being tied to a desktop, improving response times and flexibility.
knowledge_base.What training is provided?: During Phase 4 (Full Deployment & Training), comprehensive user training is conducted covering system navigation, role-specific features, best practices, troubleshooting, and process workflows. Training materials include user guides, video tutorials, and hands-on sessions to ensure effective system adoption.
knowledge_base.How is system effectiveness measured?: System effectiveness is measured by comparing KPIs before and after implementation including work order closing times, billing cycle duration, SLA compliance rates, number of delayed projects, penalty enforcement consistency, QI audit completion rates, vendor compliance scores, and user satisfaction metrics.
knowledge_base.What can a System Administrator do?: System Administrators have full access to all features and settings. They can: Manage all users and assign roles, Create, edit, and delete any project or work order, Configure system settings and SLA rules, Set up notification templates and escalation rules, Manage vendors, sectors, and all master data, View and export all reports and analytics, Access audit logs and system logs, Configure integrations and API settings, Manage penalty rules and waive penalties, Approve or override any decision in the system, Perform bulk imports and data migrations, Manage document types and workflow stages, Access all dashboards across all sectors and teams, Reset user passwords and manage security settings, Configure QI targets and performance metrics, and troubleshoot system issues.
knowledge_base.What can a Team Leader do?: Team Leaders manage their assigned teams and have oversight of team projects. They can: View and manage projects assigned to their team, Assign work orders and tasks to team members, Review and approve documents submitted by their team, Monitor team performance and productivity metrics, Approve or reject vendor submissions for their projects, View SLA compliance for their team's projects, Escalate issues to Sector Managers when needed, Assign QI inspectors to projects, Review QI inspection results for their projects, Manage team member workloads and assignments, View team-specific reports and analytics, Receive and act on first-level escalations, Approve minor penalty waivers (within authority limits), Track document compliance for team projects, Manage project milestones and timelines, and provide feedback on vendor performance for their projects.
knowledge_base.What can a Sector Manager do?: Sector Managers oversee all activities within their geographic sector. They can: View and manage all projects in their sector, Monitor performance across all teams in the sector, Review sector-wide SLA compliance and performance metrics, Approve major decisions and escalations from Team Leaders, Manage vendor relationships for the sector, Review and approve penalties for sector projects, Access sector-wide financial reports and billing status, Assign projects to teams and reallocate resources, Review and approve high-value invoices, Monitor QI performance across the sector, Analyze delay factors and trends in their sector, Approve SLA extensions and deadline modifications, Generate sector performance reports for management, Coordinate with other Sector Managers on cross-sector projects, Set sector-specific priorities and targets, Review audit logs for their sector, and provide strategic oversight of all sector operations.
knowledge_base.What can a Supervisor do?: Supervisors (WO Supervisors) manage day-to-day project execution and monitoring. They can: Create and manage work orders, Monitor project progress and status, Assign work orders to field teams and contractors, Review and approve daily work reports, Track work order completion and delays, Upload and verify project documents, Coordinate QI inspections for their projects, Review inspection results and corrective actions, Monitor SLA compliance for assigned projects, Escalate issues to Team Leaders when needed, Update project status and milestones, Manage project documentation and compliance, Verify vendor submissions and work completion, Track material usage and site progress, Coordinate with vendors and contractors, Record delay factors and reasons, Generate progress reports for management, Monitor quality and safety on projects, Approve minor document submissions, and maintain accurate project records.
knowledge_base.What can an Engineer do?: Engineers provide technical oversight and review. They can: Review technical documents and drawings, Approve design submissions and technical specifications, Conduct technical reviews of project plans, Review and approve material specifications, Provide technical guidance to field teams, Review QI inspection findings, Approve or reject technical change requests, Review vendor technical submissions, Monitor compliance with technical standards, Approve construction methodologies, Review as-built drawings and documentation, Provide technical input on delay factors, Review test results and commissioning reports, Approve technical aspects of project closeout, Generate technical reports and documentation, Review safety and quality issues from technical perspective, Approve material substitutions or changes, Coordinate with QI on technical requirements, and maintain technical documentation standards.

knowledge_base.What is the purpose of the Smart Vendor:
The Smart Vendor Monitoring System is designed to automate and streamline the vendor project management process from project initiation through completion and billing. Its main purposes are:
 (1) Eliminate delays in the work order closing process by automating document tracking and sending timely reminders,
 (2) Ensure timely vendor billing by tracking all required documents and approvals,
 (3) Improve SLA compliance through automated monitoring and escalations,
 (4) Enforce penalties consistently for non-compliance to encourage vendor accountability,
 (5) Optimize QI workload through intelligent inspection scheduling and capacity tracking,
 (6) Provide real-time visibility into project status for all stakeholders,
 (7) Enable data-driven decision making through comprehensive analytics and reporting,
 (8) Reduce manual administrative tasks through automation, and
 (9) Improve overall vendor performance and accountability.

knowledge_base.What is the project lifecycle in the sys:
Projects flow through the following stages:
 (1) Project Creation - Project is registered in the system with all basic details (code, name, vendor, sector, dates, contract value),
 (2) Planning - Requirements defined, QI assigned, SLA deadlines set, workflow stages configured,
 (3) Work Order Issuance - Work orders created and assigned to vendor,
 (4) Execution - Vendor performs work on site, progress tracked through work order updates,
 (5) Field Completion - Vendor completes physical work, prepares for inspection,

knowledge_base.What is SLA and why is it important?:
SLA stands for Service Level Agreement. It defines the maximum time allowed to complete specific tasks or milestones. In this system, SLAs are critical because:
 (1) They set clear expectations for vendors and internal teams on required turnaround times,
 (2) They ensure projects progress in a timely manner without unnecessary delays,
 (3) They enable automated tracking and alerts when deadlines are approaching or missed,
 (4) They trigger escalations to supervisors and managers when issues need attention,
 (5) They provide objective criteria for measuring vendor and internal team performance,
 (6) They form the basis for penalty calculations when vendors fail to meet deadlines,
 (7) They help management identify bottlenecks in the process,
 (8) They ensure faster project completion and billing, ultimately improving cash flow. Common SLAs in the system include: COC submission within 7 days of work completion, QI inspection within 3 days of COC submission, Document approval within 2 days of submission, Invoice generation within 5 days of final approval.
knowledge_base.What is a Certificate of Completion (COC:
A Certificate of Completion (COC) is a formal document submitted by the vendor to certify that all contracted work has been completed according to specifications. The COC is crucial because:
 (1) It serves as the vendor's official declaration that work is finished,
 (2) It triggers the QI inspection process to verify completion,
 (3) It includes detailed information about the work performed, completion date, and any issues encountered,
 (4) It must be accompanied by photos showing the completed work,
 (5) It starts the clock for billing and payment processing,
 (6) It is a required document before any invoice can be generated,
 (7) Late COC submission may result in penalties under SLA rules. A complete COC package typically includes: The signed COC form with project and work order details, Before and after photos of the work site, As-built drawings or sketches if applicable, Material usage records, Any required test results or certifications, Contractor signature and company seal. The COC submission deadline is tracked by the system and vendors receive reminders as the deadline approaches.
knowledge_base.What are delay factors and how are they:
Delay factors are the reasons why a project or task is delayed beyond its target completion date. The system tracks delay factors to:
 (1) Understand root causes of delays,
 (2) Determine responsibility (vendor vs. client vs. external),
 (3) Decide whether penalties should apply,
 (4) Identify systemic issues that need process improvements,
 (5) Provide data for trend analysis and forecasting. Common delay factors include:
 (1) Weather conditions - Rain, typhoons, extreme heat preventing safe work,
 (2) Material shortages - Delays in material availability or delivery,
 (3) Permit delays - Late approval of required permits or clearances,
 (4) Site access issues - Unable to access work site due to customer, security, or other issues,
 (5) Design changes - Changes to project scope or specifications,
 (6) Equipment failures - Breakdown of required equipment,
 (7) Manpower shortages - Insufficient skilled labor available,
 (8) Client-caused delays - Customer not available, not prepared, or requesting postponement,
 (9) Utility conflicts - Conflicts with other utilities requiring coordination,
 (10) Safety concerns - Work suspended due to unsafe conditions. When a delay occurs, the responsible party (supervisor, vendor, or engineer) records the delay factor in the system with: Date of delay, Duration in days, Category of delay, Detailed description, Supporting evidence if available, Responsible party. Delays marked as 'vendor responsibility' may result in penalties, while delays marked as 'client responsibility' or 'force majeure' typically exclude the period from SLA calculations. Delay factor reports help management identify patterns and address recurring issues.

 (10) Final Documentation - All paperwork completed and approved,
 (11) Billing Preparation - Invoice prepared and approved,
 (12) Payment Processing - Invoice sent and payment received,
 (13) Project Closure - All documentation archived. Each workflow stage has: Assigned responsible person or role (who must complete it), Target duration (how long it should take), SLA deadline (when it must be completed by), Current status (Not Started, In Progress, Completed, Blocked), Completion date and time when finished. Benefits of workflow tracking: Shows exactly where each project is in the process, Identifies bottlenecks where projects get stuck, Enables progress reporting and forecasting, Ensures nothing is skipped or forgotten, Triggers automatic notifications at each stage transition, Provides data for process improvement, Allows management to see workload at each stage across all projects.
knowledge_base.How does the system calculate penalties?:
The system calculates penalties using a combination of rule-based calculations and machine learning predictions. The penalty calculation process:
 (1) Identify the violation type: SLA Breach - Missing a deadline, Quality Issue - Failing inspection, Safety Violation - Safety rules not followed, Documentation Issue - Missing or incorrect documents, Re-work Required - Work must be redone.
 (2) Determine if penalty applies: Check if vendor is responsible for the delay (not client or force majeure), Verify the SLA or requirement was clearly defined, Check if this is a first-time minor violation (may get warning instead), Consider any approved extensions or waivers.
 (3) Calculate penalty amount using: Contract value as baseline, Number of days delayed past the SLA, Severity of the issue (minor, moderate, critical), Violation type and category, Historical precedents (similar cases), Vendor's past performance and compliance score.
 (4) Machine Learning Prediction: The ML model analyzes historical penalty data to predict appropriate penalty amounts based on similar past cases. It considers: Similar violation types, Similar contract values, Similar delay durations, Outcomes of past penalties (paid, disputed, waived), Industry standards and practices.
 (5) Apply penalty rules: Minimum penalty thresholds (e.g., delays under 2 days may not incur penalty), Maximum penalty caps (e.g., penalties cannot exceed 10% of contract value), Grace periods for first-time offenders, Escalating penalties for repeat violations.
 (6) Generate penalty memo: System creates a formal penalty notification document, Includes violation details, calculation breakdown, and payment instructions, Sent to vendor through the portal and email. Vendors can view the penalty calculation and dispute if they believe it's unfair or incorrect. All penalty calculations are logged for audit purposes.

knowledge_base.What is the penalty dispute resolution p:
When a vendor believes a penalty is unjust or incorrect, they can follow the dispute resolution process:
 (1) Vendor submits dispute through portal: Select the penalty being disputed, Choose dispute reason from categories (Incorrect facts, Force majeure circumstances, Client-caused delay, Calculation error, Unfair application of rules, Other with explanation), Provide detailed written explanation, Upload supporting evidence (photos, correspondence, third-party reports, weather data, etc.), Suggest desired resolution (Full waiver, Partial reduction, Payment plan, Other).
 (2) Dispute received and acknowledged: System automatically acknowledges receipt, Penalty status changes from 'Issued' to 'Disputed', Dispute is routed to designated reviewer (usually supervisor or manager), Vendor receives confirmation with timeline for review.
 (3) Internal review process: Assigned reviewer examines dispute and evidence, Reviews original penalty decision and calculation, May request additional information from vendor or internal team, Consults with QI, engineers, or other relevant personnel, Checks against policy and precedents, Considers vendor's overall performance and history.
 (4) Review decision options: Approve Dispute - Full Waiver: Penalty is completely waived, Vendor compliance score adjusted (penalty impact removed), If already deducted from invoice, credit note issued or next invoice adjusted, Vendor notified of approval with explanation. Partially Approve Dispute: Penalty amount reduced but not eliminated, New penalty amount calculated and communicated, Adjustment made to invoice if needed, Vendor notified of partial approval with reasoning. Deny Dispute: Penalty stands as originally issued, Detailed explanation provided to vendor, Vendor has right to appeal to higher management if policy allows, Penalty remains on vendor's record and in invoice calculations.
 (5) Appeal process (if available): If dispute denied, vendor can request escalation to senior management, Must provide additional evidence or new information, Senior management conducts final review, Decision is final and binding.
 (6) Documentation and logging: All dispute communications are logged in system, Decision rationale is documented for future reference, Dispute outcome used as precedent for similar future cases, Statistics tracked (dispute rate, approval rate, common reasons). Timeline: Disputes typically reviewed within 5-7 business days, Complex cases may take longer with notification to vendor, Urgent disputes for high-value penalties expedited. The dispute process ensures fairness and provides vendors with recourse while maintaining systematic penalty enforcement.
